_comment: Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B on the user's ComfyUI (API format): a video from a start frame (and a prompt), for video.loop. bromigos-art fills it through _meta.video and _meta.bind (comfy.rs, video.rs): the size from the asset's aspect at the resolution tier's pixel count (on the 32 px grid this model's latent node needs), the frame count from duration x fps, the seed from the asset's spec. A loop (or any end frame) is this model's end-frame trick, checked on the lab's 5090: the end image held for 5 frames is encoded and its second latent (a whole 4-frame chunk of it) replaces the last latent frame, clean (noise mask 0), so the motion comes back to it; the frames that chunk decodes to are dropped, and the clip ends on a frame next to the start, the way nolgia's end-frame loops do (glow-loop.py cuts at the wrap). Without an end frame, loop_mode = "crossfade" crossfades the clip's tail into its head instead (KJNodes' CrossFadeImages). Sampling is Comfy-Org's video_wan2_2_5B_ti2v template: 20 steps, cfg 5, uni_pc/simple, shift 8. Weights: Comfy-Org/Wan_2.2_ComfyUI_Repackaged, fetched by helm/comfyui in the homelab repo.

_meta.vram_note: ComfyUI's peak on the 5090 (32 GiB, the voice and embeddings servers resident: 13.9 GiB at rest), a 5 s loop at 768x1152, measured 2026-10-09; it takes what's free (dynamic loading), so a smaller card runs it slower rather than not at all
_meta.seconds_note: a 5 s 720p-tier loop on the 5090: 20 steps at 5.7 s, the VAE decode 16 s, loading 5 s
